items.title: Full-Body Strength A
items.description: Warm up with 5 minutes of marching and arm circles. Perform dumbbell goblet squats, dumbbell floor presses, resistance-band rows, and glute bridges with controlled movements.

items.title: Core Stability
items.description: Perform dead bugs and bird dogs slowly, keeping your back comfortable and your movements controlled.

items.title: Protein-Rich Breakfast
items.description: Eat vegetable besan chilla with curd, or oats with milk, nuts, and seeds to start the day with a balanced vegetarian meal.

items.title: Balanced Lunch
items.description: Have dal or rajma with rice or roti, a serving of vegetables, and curd or paneer for additional protein.

items.title: Post-Workout Recovery
items.description: Cool down with gentle stretches and take a short walk if comfortable. Drink water throughout the day and aim for a consistent bedtime.

items.title: Light Cardio and Mobility
items.description: Walk at a comfortable pace, then perform shoulder circles, hip circles, cat-cow movements, and gentle hamstring stretches. Keep the session easy enough to recover from Monday's workout.

items.title: Protein-Packed Snack
items.description: Choose roasted chana, a glass of milk, or plain yogurt with nuts as a convenient vegetarian snack.

items.title: Paneer or Tofu Dinner
items.description: Prepare paneer or tofu with mixed vegetables and serve it with roti or rice. Include a variety of vegetables for a balanced meal.

items.title: Hydration Routine
items.description: Keep a water bottle nearby and drink regularly throughout the day, especially around exercise and in hot weather.

items.title: Full-Body Strength B
items.description: Warm up for 5 minutes, then perform dumbbell Romanian deadlifts, supported one-arm dumbbell rows, standing dumbbell shoulder presses, and bodyweight squats. Use light weights and stop each set before your form deteriorates.

items.title: Upper-Body Band Work
items.description: Perform resistance-band pull-aparts and biceps curls with smooth, controlled movements. Choose a band that lets you complete every repetition without straining.

items.title: Balanced Breakfast
items.description: Have moong dal chilla with paneer filling or whole-grain toast with peanut butter and a glass of milk.

items.title: Protein-Rich Dinner
items.description: Serve chickpea curry or dal with rice or roti and a side of vegetables. Include curd if it suits your dietary preference.

items.title: Gentle Cooldown
items.description: Stretch your chest, shoulders, hips, and hamstrings gently after training. Breathe steadily and avoid bouncing during stretches.

items.title: Active Recovery Walk
items.description: Take an easy outdoor walk and keep the pace conversational. If you feel tired, shorten the walk and prioritize recovery rather than adding extra exercise.

items.title: Gentle Mobility
items.description: Practice cat-cow, shoulder rolls, gentle hip-flexor stretches, and ankle circles. Move only through a comfortable range without forcing any position.

items.title: Vegetarian Protein Bowl
items.description: Combine cooked chickpeas or rajma, rice, chopped vegetables, and curd or tofu for a filling, balanced meal.

items.title: Sleep Consistency
items.description: Set a regular bedtime and reduce stimulating screen use before sleep. Allow enough time for approximately 7-9 hours of sleep.

items.title: Full-Body Strength C
items.description: Warm up for 5 minutes, then perform dumbbell goblet squats, dumbbell floor presses, dumbbell Romanian deadlifts, and resistance-band rows. Use a manageable load and rest between sets.

items.title: Glute and Core Finisher
items.description: Perform glute bridges and dead bugs with controlled breathing. Keep the effort moderate and skip any movement that causes discomfort.

items.title: Muscle-Supporting Breakfast
items.description: Eat oats prepared with milk and nuts, or poha served with a side of curd and roasted chana.

items.title: Balanced Post-Workout Meal
items.description: Have tofu or paneer with rice or roti and vegetables after training, or choose dal with rice and curd. Eat a satisfying meal that fits your appetite.

items.title: Track Your Progress
items.description: Record the exercises, dumbbell weights, sets, and repetitions you completed. Aim to improve gradually while maintaining good technique.

items.title: Optional Light Activity
items.description: Choose a relaxed walk, easy cycling, or a recreational activity you enjoy. Keep the intensity low and skip the session if you need more recovery.

items.title: Protein-Rich Vegetarian Lunch
items.description: Prepare a meal with soy chunks, paneer, tofu, or lentils alongside rice or roti and seasonal vegetables.

items.title: Nutritious Snack
items.description: Choose milk, yogurt, roasted chickpeas, sprouts, or a small handful of nuts between meals according to your hunger.

items.title: Meal Preparation
items.description: Prepare a batch of dal, beans, boiled chickpeas, or chopped vegetables to make balanced vegetarian meals easier during the coming week.

items.title: Rest and Recovery
items.description: Take a full rest day from strength training. Gentle walking and comfortable stretching are optional if they help you feel relaxed.

items.title: Balanced Vegetarian Breakfast
items.description: Choose idli with sambar, vegetable upma with curd, or besan chilla with paneer. Include a protein source as part of your usual breakfast.

items.title: Wholesome Family Meal
items.description: Build your meal around dal, beans, tofu, paneer, or another vegetarian protein, with vegetables and rice or roti. Include different foods across the day for variety.

items.title: Weekly Reflection
items.description: Review your workout log, note which exercises felt comfortable, and prepare your equipment for the next week. Increase weights or repetitions only when your current routine feels manageable with good form.

items.title: Prepare for Quality Sleep
items.description: Keep your evening routine calm, avoid late caffeine if it affects your sleep, and aim for a consistent bedtime.
